newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates drop further on bank lending.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates drop further on bank lending.

text.p: Interbank rates dropped further on Tuesday due to lending by big banks which now have excess funds, dealers said.
"Some of the big banks are long and they are still lending," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. He said banks had reversed their earlier short position due to recent borrowings and bills maturities.
One-week money was at 7.20 percent against 7.40 percent on Monday, dealers said.
One-month money was at 7.55 percent and three-month money at 7.60 percent. They were at 7.60/80 percent on Monday.

Dealers said rates have been pressured by improved liquidity following recent lending by the central bank and last week's maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 1.5 billion ringgit which were not rolled over.
There will be another maturity of a 500-million ringgit bill issue on Wednesday.

But dealers said an outflow of some two billion ringgit on Thursday due to maturity of funds Bank Negara lent to the market to help ease market tightness last month, could prevent rates from falling further.
"I expect the one-month to stabilise around 7.5 percent as there are no new Bank Negara bills issue to roll-over the maturities," one dealer said.
The overnight rate, which fell to 5.8/6.0 percent on Monday, was expected to trade around 6.0 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange stayed firm on the back of softening in cash interbank rates.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up three points to 92.58, or an implied yield of 7.42 percent.
The December contract rose two to 92.68, or 7.32 percent and March 1998 was up three to 92.76, or 7.24 percent.
